card.name: Setting up a logical conclusion with 'it'
card.fires_on: The word 'it' (or 'stands', 'does not', 'logically') right after a premise, where the next words draw a conclusion such as 'follows', 'means' or 'stands to reason'.

modes.label: 'it' before a conclusion
modes.description: 'it' starts the clause that draws an inference after a stated premise.
modes.example: We have already seen that castles were a feature of feudalism so<< it>> follows that the Normans introduced castles

modes.label: 'stands' in 'stands to reason'
modes.description: The verb 'stands' in the idiom that introduces a reasoned conclusion.
modes.example: so it<< stands>> to reason that the ‘founding fathers

modes.label: 'not' after 'it does'
modes.description: 'not' in 'it does not mean/appear', which denies an implied inference.
modes.example: it does<< not>> mean it will be no good.

card.writes: It pushes the model to predict 'follow' or 'follows', as in 'it follows that'.
card.plain: It fires where a sentence is about to say that one thing follows from, or does not follow from, another.
